# Sirach Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_007_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Do no evil, and no evil will come your way.

**2** Stay away from wrong, and wrong will stay away from you.

**3** Don't plant seeds of injustice — the harvest you reap will be seven times worse.

**4** Don't go to the Lord looking for special status, or to a king expecting a seat of honor.

**5** Don't try to justify yourself before God, and don't try to look clever before the king.

**6** Don't pursue a judgeship unless you have the backbone to confront injustice. You might end up showing favoritism to someone powerful and ruining your own reputation.

**7** Don't do things that shame you before your whole city. Don't embarrass yourself in a public assembly.

**8** Don't let yourself repeat a sin — even doing it once has its consequences.

**9** Don't think you can just pile on the offerings and say, "God will notice all these gifts and accept them."

**10** Don't pray half-heartedly. Don't forget to give to those in need.

**11** Don't make fun of someone whose heart is breaking. Remember: it is God who brings people low and lifts them up.

**12** Don't scheme against your brother. Don't plot against a friend or neighbor.

**13** Don't lie — ever. The habit of lying takes you nowhere good.

**14** Don't talk too much in the company of the elders. Don't repeat yourself when you pray.

**15** Don't despise hard work. Don't look down on farming — God himself established it.

**16** Don't start thinking of yourself as one of the sinners — remember, God's anger doesn't take long.

**17** Lower yourself. Really lower yourself. The fate that awaits the ungodly is fire and worms.

**18** Don't trade a friend for money. Don't swap a true brother for gold.

**19** Don't let go of a wife who is wise and kind — she is worth more than gold.

**20** Don't be cruel to a servant who is loyal and hardworking. Don't take advantage of a laborer who gives you everything they have.

**21** Treat a capable servant like a close friend. Don't hold back their freedom.

**22** If you have animals, take care of them. If they're earning their keep, hold on to them.

**23** If you have children, discipline them. Start shaping their character from the time they are young.

**24** If you have daughters, keep watch over them. Don't be so permissive that you regret it later.

**25** Getting your daughter married well is a major achievement — just make sure you give her to a man with good sense.

**26** If you have a wife, don't cast her aside. But don't put your confidence in a woman you've come to resent.

**27** Honor your father with everything in you. And don't forget how much your mother suffered to bring you into the world.

**28** They are the reason you exist. What could you possibly give them that would come close to repaying what they gave you?

**29** Fear the Lord with everything you have, and hold his priests in deep respect.

**30** Love your Creator with all your strength, and don't neglect those who serve him.

**31** Honor the Lord and honor his priests — give them what is rightly theirs: the firstfruits, the sin offering, the shoulder portion, the sacrifices, and the firstfruits of the holy things.

**32** Don't forget the poor either — your generosity to them completes your blessing.

**33** Be generous to everyone while they are alive. And don't withdraw your kindness even from the dead.

**34** Don't turn away from people who are crying. Sit with those who are in mourning.

**35** Don't hesitate to visit people who are sick. These are exactly the kinds of acts that make people love you.

**36** Whatever you do, keep the end of your life in view — and you will never sin.
